overview.description: 66 German (Sechsundsechzig): two-player trick-taking. 24-card deck (A-10-K-Q-J-9). 6 cards each; turned card for trump. First to 66 trick points (and declare) wins the hand. Marriages (K+Q same suit) 20 or 40; close stock to force follow suit. Game to 7 match points.

history.origins: German two-player game (Sechsundsechzig); said to originate around 1652 in Paderborn. Related to Schnapsen (Austria).
timeline: 1652: Tradition holds that Sixty-Six (Sechsundsechzig) was first played in Paderborn, Westphalia, where a commemorative plaque now marks the site.
19th century: Documented in German card-game compendia as a shortened 24-card Mariage variant that allows a player to go out on reaching 66 points.
20th century: Becomes a staple two-player tavern game across Germany, while the closely related Schnapsen variant gains national-game status in Austria.

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.

setup.dealing:
Cards per Player: 6
Dealing Pattern: Dealer shuffles and deals 6 cards to each player (in packets or singly), then turns the next card face up to set the trump suit and places the remaining 11 cards crosswise on top as the stock (talon).

rules.objective: Be first to 66 trick points in a hand (and declare) or reach 7 match points.
rules.gameplay: 6 cards each; trump from turn-up. Play tricks; marriages 20/40; close stock to force follow suit. First to 66 and declare wins hand; 7 match points wins game.

strategy.basic: Declare marriages when safe; close stock when you can make 66.
strategy.intermediate: Count trick points; hold trump 9 (nine of trumps) for key tricks.
strategy.advanced: When to exchange turn-up for 9; force follow by closing stock.
tips: Stock closed = must follow suit when possible.

list.name: Three-player 66
list.description: Three-handed game in which all 24 cards are dealt out, eight to each player. One player chooses trumps from an initial three-card packet, there is no talon, players must follow suit and try to win tricks, and marriages still score 20 or 40 while the aim remains to reach 66 card points.

list.description: Partnership variant where two teams of two play with a 24-card pack and aim for 66 points as a side. Sources describe adjusted dealing, trump selection, and partnership scoring but retain the same marriage and trick-point structure as the base game.

drawSources.notes: After each trick while the stock remains, the trick winner draws the top card from the talon and the opponent then draws the next card so both hands return to six cards.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: During the second phase and after closing the talon, players must follow suit and win the trick if possible; trumps beat any non-trump.

engine.deckDescription: A stripped 24-card deck built from a standard French-suited pack by removing ranks 2 through 8 so that each of the four suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) contains only ace, ten, king, queen, jack, and nine. This short deck is traditional for 66 and concentrates card points into a small number of cards.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits are used: hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades. Either suit can be trump, chosen each hand by the turned-up card from the talon, and players follow or trump according to the phase of play.
engine.rankDescription: Six ranks per suit: ace (high), ten, king, queen, jack, and nine (low). Card-point values are A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 9=0, and these points plus marriage bonuses and last-trick bonus are used to reach the 66-point target.
